newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Telefonica 9-month net seen up 22 pct.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Telefonica 9-month net seen up 22 pct.

text.p: Spain's Telefonica nine-month net profit should rise 21.7 percent to 122.22 billion pesetas due to a sharp rise in demand for mobile phones and good results overseas, a consensus among five analysts showed on Tuesday.

"The number of mobile phones rose sharply in Spain and Telefonica Internacional (TISA) will bring another 20 billion pesetas in the first nine months of the year, which compares with 12 billion pesetas in the first semester of the year," said Inigo Vega at Credit Lyonnais.

The telecommunications group -- in which the Spanish state plans to sell its 21 percent stake at the beginning of 1997 -- should end the full year with a 20 percent rise in its net profit to 160 billion pesetas.
It is expected to report nine-month figures later this week.

"Apart from the number of new mobile phones, we don't have many figures. But we would rule out any big surprises: the company's results to September should be in line with the expected growth of 20 percent for the full year," said Luis Prota of Asesores Bursatiles.
The firm had already confirmed that its revenues were in line with telephone usage and that they were ruling out any surprises, echoed Alberto Arroyo at BBV Interactivos.
Inigo Vega forecast Telefonica sales to be up 13 percent to 1,470 billion pesetas in the first nine months.
By September, Telefonica showed 466,000 subscriptions to its new satellite mobile phones (MOVISTAR, GSM), which were launched in autumn 1995.

Although one analyst said Telefonica's traditional business -- stripping out overseas and mobile phone profit boosts -- should rise a moderate seven percent, many were positive on the longer-term outlook for the group.

The green light it recently received from the European Commission to integrate its operation with Unisorce will give it direct access to new markets. The Commission announced its decision at the beginning of November after Spain promised to liberalise its telecommunications market on December 1, 1998.
Even though Telefonica pulled out of its cable television venture, the firm is set to launch digital television after March 1997.

Telefonica shares have reflected these positive forecasts. Since the beginning of 1996 they have gained 61.3 percent to a new record high on Tuesday of 2,710 pesetas, far outstripping the overall market.
